# Adviser Use commission-category modal: three confirmed regressions (AC01, AC04, AC10/AC14)

> **Status:** Draft · not yet filed in a tracker
> **Severity:** Medium-High — three independent, confirmed mismatches against the "Select
> Default Commission Category" user story within the same Adviser Use modal. None error
> out or block the quote; each is a silent behavior gap versus the documented spec.
> **Component:** Quote › Adviser Use (Commissions modal)
> **Environment:** `outsystems-dev.asteronlife.co.nz` (Asteron Connect Quote & Apply, "Illustration" step)
> **Found via:** Automated test (Playwright) — `apps/asteron-quote-apply/tests/quote-screen/select-default-commission-category-part-1.spec.js`
> and `part-2.spec.js` — then independently re-verified with two fresh, minimal probe
> scripts per the project's "verify with a different script" rule:
> `apps/asteron-quote-apply/probes/probe-ic-rc-autoselect-recheck.js` and
> `probe-ac01-label-and-ac04-update-button-recheck.js`
> **Reported:** 2026-08-25 · automated user-story regression suite + live interactive follow-up

## Summary

Running the full "Select Default Commission Category" user-story suite (Parts 1-2; Part 3
is separately, already-documented as expected-to-fail — see its own file header) surfaced
three distinct mismatches against `docs/business-rules/quote-screen/adviser-use-commission/page.md`.
All three were re-confirmed independently — a second, minimal probe script using its own
DOM reads (not the shared `adviser-use-helpers.js` functions the spec files use), plus a
zero-interaction timing re-sample for the one that most resembles a previously-retracted
false positive — so none of these are being reported off a single run or a shared-helper bug.

1. **AC01 — the "Default for Agency (\<agency numbers\>)" label no longer shows any
   agency number.** It now reads literally "Default for Agency" with nothing in
   parentheses, confirmed both in the raw DOM text and visually via screenshot.
2. **AC04 — the Update button starts enabled, not disabled**, on a completely fresh
   Adviser Use open with zero prior interaction. This is superficially the same shape as
   a false positive retracted earlier this project (caused by a banned
   `page.mouse.wheel()` call) — but today's re-check used neither that nor any other
   interaction before reading the button state, and reproduced it cleanly twice
   (immediately, and again 3 seconds later with zero interaction in between).
3. **AC10/AC14 — Select IC/RC no longer auto-selects the single Upfront-valid option**
   at Flexi Rates 2.5%, 7.5%, and 15% (each has exactly one option in its list that's
   valid for the Upfront category, which should auto-select per AC14) — it now stays on
   "Please Select" at all three. The mechanism isn't fully dead, though: Flexi Rate N/A
   (trivially one option, period) still auto-selects correctly, and Flexi Rate 12.5%
   (multiple Upfront-valid options — auto-select should NOT happen, per AC15) correctly
   still stays on "Please Select" too. So specifically the "pick the one Upfront-valid
   option out of several listed" logic looks broken, not the whole feature.

## Preconditions

A logged-in adviser session, on a **fresh, priced quote** (Age 35, Gender Male,
Occupation Code AA, Life cover with Sum Insured $500,000 — **all just-needs-to-be-valid**,
not specific-and-required; the quote only needs to price successfully so Adviser Use has
something to act on). Opening **Adviser Use** from the quote footer. For finding 3, the
quote-level **Flexi Rate** field must be set to the specific value under test (N/A/2.5%/
7.5%/15%/12.5% — **specific-and-required**, since that's literally the variable under
test) and must be set **before** opening Adviser Use, on its own fresh quote per value —
reusing one quote across Flexi Rate values is a documented stateful-carryover trap
unrelated to this finding, so a fresh quote per value rules it out.

## Steps to reproduce

**Finding 1 (AC01):**
1. Open a fresh priced quote, open Adviser Use.
2. Read the label above the "Default for Agency" dropdown.
   - **Expected** (per `ADV-01`): `"Default for Agency (\<real agency numbers\>)"`.
   - **Actual**: `"Default for Agency"` — no parenthetical content at all.

**Finding 2 (AC04):**
1. Open a fresh priced quote, open Adviser Use.
2. Immediately (zero clicks, zero field changes) read the Update button's `disabled` state.
   - **Expected** (per `AC04`/`ADV-07`): `disabled = true`.
   - **Actual**: `disabled = false` — confirmed again after a further 3-second wait with
     no interaction, ruling out a timing race.

**Finding 3 (AC10/AC14):**
1. On a fresh quote, set Flexi Rate to **2.5%**, then open Adviser Use.
2. Read the "Select IC/RC" dropdown's selected option.
   - **Expected** (per `ADV-08`): auto-selected to `"IC-100%, RC-50%"` (the only
     Upfront-valid option among the 2 listed).
   - **Actual**: stays on `"Please Select"`.
3. Repeat on fresh quotes at **7.5%** (expected `"IC-75%, RC-100%"`, `ADV-09`) and
   **15%** (expected `"IC-50%, RC-50%"`, `ADV-10`) — same result, stays unselected.
4. **Controls, both behaving correctly:** Flexi Rate **N/A** (only one option exists at
   all) still auto-selects it; Flexi Rate **12.5%** (4 options, more than one valid for
   Upfront) correctly stays on "Please Select" per `AC15`/`ADV-11`.

## Root cause

Unknown from black-box observation alone. For finding 3, the fact that both the trivial
single-option case (N/A) and the correctly-ambiguous case (12.5%) still behave correctly
suggests the overall "does the list have zero/one/many Upfront-valid options" branching
logic is intact, but whatever step resolves "which specific listed option is the
Upfront-valid one, when there's more than one option in the list" appears broken — a
narrower fault than "auto-select is off," which is consistent with N/A (never had more
than one listed option to disambiguate among) being unaffected. Findings 1 and 2 have no
obvious shared mechanism with finding 3 or each other beyond both living in the same
modal — no console/network errors were observed for any of the three.

## Reproducibility

- **AC01**: confirmed on 2 independent runs (the spec-file run, and the standalone
  re-check probe), both showing the label with no agency number.
- **AC04**: confirmed on 2 independent runs (the spec-file run, and the standalone
  re-check probe) — the probe additionally re-sampled after a 3-second zero-interaction
  wait to rule out a timing race, per the "if the behavior could plausibly be
  time-dependent" rule. No variance.
- **AC10/AC14 (2.5%/7.5%/15%)**: confirmed on 2 independent runs each (the spec-file run
  for 2.5%/7.5%/15%, and the standalone re-check probe covering all 5 Flexi Rate values
  including the two controls) — full agreement across both methods on all 5 values.

## Possible explanations to rule out first

- **A real regression** — most likely for all three, given each reproduced cleanly on an
  independently-written probe using different code from the spec file's shared helpers,
  ruling out a helper-level bug producing the same wrong reading twice.
- **An intentional change** — worth checking with a BA/PM, particularly for AC01 (maybe
  the agency number was deliberately dropped from the label for a redesign reason not
  yet documented) — less plausible for AC04 (a starts-enabled Update button that silently
  lets an adviser change a shared agency-wide setting without an explicit edit looks like
  a real defect, not a deliberate UX choice) or finding 3 (a *partially* broken
  auto-select, correct at the edges but wrong in the middle, doesn't read like a
  deliberate design change).
- **A test artifact** — ruled out for all three via the independent re-check probes,
  which use different code paths from the shared `adviser-use-helpers.js` functions the
  spec files call, and (for AC04 specifically) explicitly avoid the exact interaction
  pattern (`page.mouse.wheel()`) that caused an earlier, superficially similar false
  positive in this same modal.

## Suggested next step

Confirm with a BA/PM whether any of these three were intentional. If not, file as defects
with the dev team using this report — they may or may not share a root cause, but are
independently confirmed regardless. Once resolved either way, update
`docs/business-rules/quote-screen/adviser-use-commission/page.md`
(`ADV-01`, `ADV-07`, `ADV-08`/`ADV-09`/`ADV-10`) and the corresponding spec-file
assertions to match.
